name: MAX9031AXK+T
title: Low-cost one-, two- and four-channel single-supply comparators with built-in hysteresis
summary: The MAX9030, MAX9031, MAX9032 and MAX9034 hold one, one, two and four comparators. They run from a single +2.5 V to +5.5 V supply or from split supplies of ±1.25 V to ±2.75 V, draw 35 µA typical per comparator and switch in 188 ns typical. Each has 4 mV of internal hysteresis, inputs that reach down to the negative rail and up to 1.1 V below the positive rail, and an output that swings rail to rail. Only the MAX9030 has a shutdown pin. The MAX9031AXK+T is the single comparator without shutdown in the 5-pin SC70.

circuits.title: Additional hysteresis
circuits.description: The signal goes to IN-, and IN+ sits on a divider between a reference and the output: R2 from VREF, R1 from OUT. Positive feedback through R1 moves the IN+ threshold with the output state, so the two trip points VTH and VTL straddle VREF and the gap between them adds to the internal 4 mV.

parts.note: feedback from OUT; 100 kΩ in the worked example
from VREF; 1 kΩ in the worked example

circuits.title: Time averaging of the input signal for data recovery
circuits.description: The input drives IN+ directly and IN- through a 10 kΩ / 0.1 µF low-pass, so IN- holds the running average of the signal. The comparator then slices the data about its own mean level, which keeps the threshold centred. The RC corner must sit far below the data's carrier frequency.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: A threshold detector: R1 and R2 form a divider from the VIN line to ground and set VREF at IN-, while VIN reaches IN+. OUT drives a load RL to ground, and VDD is decoupled with 0.1 µF.

equations.name: Upper trip point (added hysteresis)

where.VTH: input level where OUT switches low on a rising VIN
where.VREF: reference voltage at the end of R2
where.VDD: positive supply, the output high level
where.R1: feedback resistor from OUT to IN+

equations.note: Assumes the output swings fully to the rails; a heavily loaded output shifts the result.

where.VTL: input level where OUT switches high on a falling VIN

equations.name: Hysteresis band
equations.expr: VHYS = VTH - VTL = VDD × R2 / (R1 + R2)

where.VHYS: width of the added hysteresis band

equations.note: Worked case: VDD = +5 V, VREF = +2.5 V, R2 = 1 kΩ and VHYS = 50 mV give R1 ≈ 100 kΩ, VTH = 2.525 V and VTL = 2.475 V.

where.fCAR: carrier frequency (fundamental) of the data stream
where.C1: averaging capacitor from IN- to ground (0.1 µF)

operation.text: MAX9030: one comparator with shutdown. MAX9031: one comparator. MAX9032: two. MAX9034: four. None but the MAX9030 has a shutdown input.

Single supply +2.5 V to +5.5 V, or split ±1.25 V to ±2.75 V. Supply current is 35 µA typical per comparator. The input common-mode range runs from the negative rail up to 1.1 V under the positive rail. An overdriven input does not reverse the output phase.
Each comparator has 4 mV of hysteresis built in, which keeps the output switching cleanly and free of oscillation even when the input moves slowly.
The output swings rail to rail. Its design keeps the current pulse drawn from the supply during a transition small, so switching puts very little glitch on the supply rail.

Pulling SHDN to 0.3 × VDD or lower shuts the part down: supply current falls from 35 µA to 0.05 µA typical and OUT goes high impedance. SHDN at 0.7 × VDD or higher runs the part normally; tie SHDN to VDD when shutdown is not used. The SHDN input is high impedance, drawing about 0.1 µA when held at VSS or VDD.

More hysteresis than the internal 4 mV comes from two resistors giving positive feedback from OUT to IN+ (the added-hysteresis circuit). Choose R2, choose the band VHYS, then solve VHYS = VDD × R2 / (R1 + R2) for R1. The trip points follow the output voltage, so the equations assume a rail-to-rail swing.

Start with 100 nF of supply bypass. Keep signal traces short to hold stray capacitance down, and keep capacitive coupling from OUT back to IN- low. For an input that rises slower than 1 ms, place 1 nF across IN+ and IN-.

In the data-recovery circuit the comparator weighs the input against a running RC average of that same input, so the switching threshold settles at the mean input level, which gives the widest noise margin; data that has passed through a path limited in bandwidth and amplitude comes out clean even with heavy phase distortion. The RC corner, 1 / (2π × R1 × C1), is chosen far below the carrier frequency.
